summary: Huawen Bai was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He studied at Peking University from circa 1951 to 1955 and served as a professor there, attested in 1999.

Hubert Decleer worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Koninklijk Atheneum Oostende, Hotel- en Toerismeschool Spermalie, and KU Leuven under Étienne Lamotte. He held positions at the School for International Training, Middlebury College, and the University of Vienna.

Hubert Durt specialized in Buddhist studies, studying under Étienne Lamotte from circa 1960 to 1970. He held posts at the École française d'Extrême-Orient, Hōbōgirin Institute, Mélanges chinois et bouddhiques, and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Hugh B. Urban works in religious studies and Indology. He completed his doctoral studies under Wendy Doniger, Bruce Lincoln, and Tony K. Stewart, and served as an associate professor at Ohio State University from circa 2003 to 2008.
Hugh Gray was an Indologist who studied at Battersea Grammar School and held a post at the University of Cambridge, attested in 1983.

Hugh J. Silverman was a philosopher who studied at Stanford University from circa 1968 to 1973. He held academic posts at the University of Vienna, the University of Klagenfurt, and the University of Turin.
Hugh Richardson was a scholar in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He studied at Keble College from circa 1924 to 1928 and served in the Indian Civil Service between circa 1930 and 1950.

Hugo David is an Indologist and philosopher who earned his PhD from the École Pratique des Hautes Études in 2012, studying with several traditional teachers. He held a fellowship at the University of Cambridge and became a permanent member of EFEO in 2015.
Hui-tzu Lu is a scholar of Sinology and history and archaeology. Lu studied under Jing-shen Tao and with traditional teachers Zhiru Shi and Zhihui Shi, both attested in 2003.
Huidi Zeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yi-hsun Huang, attested in 2011.

Huimin is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Taipei National University of the Arts, Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies, and served as president of Dharma Drum Buddhist College from circa 2007 to 2014.
Huishan Lin is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Fo Guang University under Kuo-wei Liu, and studied under teachers Mansheng, Miaoguan, and Ruying.
Huiwen Zhuang is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned an MA at Fo Guang University under Kirill Jurievitch Solonin, and studied under traditional teacher Hsing Yun.
Huiyu Zhang works in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. Zhang studied at the University of Tokyo and held a lecturer position at Dongguk University, attested in 1996.

Humberto Maturana was a scholar of philosophy who studied at Liceo Manuel de Salas, University College London, and Harvard University. He held a post at the University of Chile from circa 1960 to 2000.
Hung-Yi Yang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at the University of Sydney under the supervision of Mark Allon.

Huston Smith was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at Central Methodist University and the University of Chicago. He held positions at MIT, UC Berkeley, and Syracuse University.
Huynh Thi Ha Vy is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Kapila Abhayawansa and earned a Master of Arts at International Buddhist College, attested in 2015.

Hyejeong Choi is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at Ohio State University under John C. Huntington. Choi held a visiting researcher post at the Archaeological Institute of Kashihara, Nara Prefecture.

Hyon Gak Sunim is a Buddhist studies practitioner and scholar who studied at Yale University, the University of Freiburg, and Harvard University, as well as under traditional teacher Seungsahn from circa 1990 to 2004.
